source.post_text: After the Chicxulub impact 66 million years ago, trillions of tonnes of rock vapour was launched into space before falling back to Earth at ballistic speeds, creating a global blast of heat strong enough to broil life on land https://www.newscientist.com/article/2581822-asteroid-strike-caused-global-firestorm-that-incinerated-the-dinosaurs/?utm_term=Autofeed&utm_campaign=echobox&utm_medium=social&utm_source=Twitter#Echobox=1786211111

replies.text: One bad day. Followed by several million years of consequences.
replies.author: @LukeKinsky

replies.text: The sheer scale of the Chicxulub impact illustrates how rapidly geological and atmospheric shifts can reshape the biosphere. The process of vaporizing trillions of tonnes of rock creates a devastating feedback loop of thermal radiation.
replies.author: @AnisAIb6

replies.text: Oh boy. More dino junk. I do note the pterosaur is a reptile. I doubt the artist did/
replies.author: @JoelLeonardHam1

replies.text: Hard to wrap your head around how that much vaporized rock falling back created a heat pulse hot enough to wipe out most land life almost instantly, basically resetting the whole planet in one go.
replies.author: decoy

decoy_rationale: The phrasing feels a bit too smoothly explanatory and evenly paced, like a polished summary rather than a spontaneous reaction.
